newsitem.title: USA: USDA sees less karnal bunt threat this year.
newsitem.headline: USDA sees less karnal bunt threat this year.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said on Tuesday that karnal bunt fungus appeared to be less of a problem this year than last and the government would treat farmers fairly on the issue.

The fungus, which does not pose a health risk but spoils milling quality of grain, prompted a government quarantine of some Southwest and Western states when it was detected in the United States for the first time last year in Arizona durum seed.
But the fungus "is less of a serious problem than we might have thought a year or two ago," Glickman told reporters after speaking at a Tufts University agricultural conference.
"Our job is to make sure we treat producers around the country in a fair and equitable way," Glickman added. "Our activities are going to be fair across the board."
